verdict: A credible plumbing site with a working booking path, but the estimate form and response expectations leak ready-to-buy jobs.

leaks.title: Mobile estimate form is difficult to complete
leaks.what: Six fields, one missing label, and weak autocomplete on phone and ZIP.
leaks.evidence: Six fields; submit is visible, so the form works but is harder than needed.
leaks.why: Extra fields and unclear inputs lower completion on a phone.
leaks.fix: Cut it to name, phone, ZIP, and problem; add autocomplete and labels.

leaks.title: New inquiries have no observable immediate acknowledgement
leaks.what: The form says only "We will be in touch soon." No time, channel, or hours are promised.
leaks.evidence: The form area has generic contact language; the header hours are not connected to a response.
leaks.why: A homeowner who submits at 6pm cannot tell whether anyone saw it.
leaks.fix: Add one line beside the button: "We call or text within 15 minutes during office hours."

leaks.title: Unclosed estimates may not receive follow-up
leaks.what: The site can show an estimate request exists. It cannot show what happens next.
leaks.evidence: No public page exposes the estimate pipeline, follow-up cadence, or close rate. It is not scored.
leaks.why: Open estimates are often the largest recoverable revenue pool.
leaks.fix: Pull the open-estimate list, segment by age and value, and assign a follow-up cadence.

strengths: Phone and click-to-call are consistent on mobile, including a sticky action.
A working scheduler shows live availability and is two taps from the home page.
License, insurance, and a manufacturer certification are visible.

fixes.fix: Simplify the mobile estimate form and add input autocomplete
Publish a callback promise with a time, channel, and hours
Add a starting-at price range for the top three jobs
Use one company name and one verifiable differentiator
Add form and call conversion events

fixNote: The first two fixes are a one-afternoon pass. They recover about 5 points and remove the two highest-friction moments in the lead path.

ownerData.title: Speed-to-lead
ownerData.why: Response time drives booking rate, and the public site cannot prove it.
questions: What is the median lead-to-response time?

ownerData.title: Estimate follow-up
ownerData.why: Open estimates are the fastest recovery pool.
questions: How many estimates are open, and what is their value?

ownerData.title: Reactivation
ownerData.why: Past customers can produce jobs without new ad spend.
questions: How many customers are inactive for 12+ months?

nextSteps: This week: simplify the estimate form and add the callback promise.
Next two weeks: publish a starting-at price range and fix the mismatched company name.
Before more ad spend: add conversion events and pull the open-estimate list.

executiveSummary: Acme Plumbing has the hard parts: a consistent phone path, a working scheduler, visible licensing, and basic analytics.
The biggest observable leak is form friction on mobile, followed by a missing response expectation after submission.
The largest unknown is estimate follow-up. It is presented as an owner-data opportunity, not a website penalty.
Fix the form and the callback promise first; they are cheap, fast, and directly on the path to a booked job.
